artboards.title: A · reference card ratio, full titles
B · reference card ratio, short titles

annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards — proportions measured off your PowerPoint. Against its 315x161 red card: card height 0.51 of its width, screenshot 0.53 of the card width, top overhang 0.47 of the card height, left overhang 0.063 of the card width, front screenshot inset 0.098 of the card width, back one dropped 0.05 of the card height, gradient 0.67 of the card height.
The fan is -8 and -3: the steep version's five degrees of separation, both rotated clockwise so the front screenshot sits near upright.
The gradient is a layer on the card, so it stops at the card outline, rounded corners included. The sliver of screenshot still hanging off the left below it stays unscrimmed, as in your deck.

What the four vary, and why B exists.
At the reference card ratio a 166px-wide card is only 88px tall, and your card titles are exact-match SEO phrases: "Custom Pokédex Builder" wraps to two lines and the copy then fills almost the whole card, leaving screenshot visible only in the overhang above it. That is A.
B keeps the same card and swaps in short display titles — "Dex Builder", the way your deck labels it — which is what makes the reference's balance land. The full phrase can still live in the markup for search without being the visible label.
C and D keep the full titles and buy the room back by making the card taller: 112 and 130 against the reference's 88. D also carries the largest screenshots.

The other two widths, both at the reference card ratio with the full titles. The cards are wider here, so the same titles cost proportionally less height than they do at 390.
Desktop is the four mobile cards side by side, not a two-by-two.
